text: With the project brief approved, this lesson builds the actual orchestration layer — the state machine, the batched submission strategy, and the job-lifecycle handling that will run the eighty-iteration VQE loop for real.

Following Chapter 3's model, each iteration's submission moves through explicit states: pending, queued, running, aggregating, done — or failed, triggering a retry decision that either resubmits to a new device or falls back. Each state is persisted, so a restart resumes from the last completed iteration instead of silently re-running the whole thing and re-incurring cost.

And here's where this gets built for real — Amazon Braket's actual Hybrid Jobs wizard. This five-step flow is literally where this orchestration layer gets configured and launched against a real account.

Step one of that wizard: the algorithm itself. Script upload, entry point, hyperparameters — this is where the orchestration code you've been reading about for four chapters actually lives, as a real file.

Step four: execution configuration. Quantum and classical compute settings, side by side — exactly where the simulator-first, hardware-second verification plan gets set before a single dollar is spent on real hardware.

The orchestration code builds all thirteen shifted circuits per iteration and submits them as one program-set job, polling on a five-second schedule rather than blocking — the same pattern that scales to running this for multiple molecules later without a rewrite. And before touching Rigetti Ankaa-3 at all, the full eighty-iteration loop runs against a classical simulator, with a test harness forcing one submission to fail, confirming the state machine handles it correctly at zero cost.
Next lesson adds the two things this system needs before it can be trusted to run unattended: proper error handling, and a live, trustworthy cost ledger.
